weaknesses: Saturday morning is operationally very compressed: sleep ends at 07:30, breakfast is 07:30-07:50, travel to the football match is 07:50-08:15, and Marta must be ready for an 08:30 match. The calendar has little visible margin for waking, dressing children, hygiene, football kit checks, or delays, even though Friday packing helps.

The Saturday afternoon sequence depends on precise hand-offs: Duarte's nap ends at 15:00, travel to the birthday party is 15:10-15:30, travel from party to coffee starts immediately at 15:30, coffee is 16:00-17:00, travel to collect Marta is 17:00-17:30, and travel home is 17:30-17:50. This may work, but it leaves almost no visible margin for drop-off/check-in, collection, a tired child after nap, or delay at the trampoline park.

The plan itself identifies that the coffee is only operational if Duarte can accompany the user, but the resulting calendar still relies on that condition without confirmation. That is a material uncertainty because the partner is on a fixed shift from 13:00-21:00 on Saturday.

Sunday afternoon is a high-load chain: travel to lunch 12:20-13:00, birthday lunch 13:00-15:30, travel home 15:30-16:10, science project 16:10-17:40, long run 17:45-19:15, then dinner at 19:30. The immediate transition from family event to school project, then to a 90-minute run, leaves very little visible recovery, setup, shower, or dinner preparation margin.

The science project is due Monday and needs about 90 minutes, but it is scheduled immediately after returning from the birthday lunch. If the project requires materials, drying time, cleanup, or a child who is still able to focus after a long social outing, the calendar may be fragile.
The rationale says groceries include Sunday dessert ingredients, but the visible calendar does not show any time to prepare the dessert before the grandfather's birthday lunch.
